newsitem.title: USA: Gingrich says Clinton may undermine welfare reform.
newsitem.headline: Gingrich says Clinton may undermine welfare reform.

text.p: House Speaker Newt Gingrich suggested Friday that the White House was trying to undermine welfare reform and said Congress may stage a counterattack after it returns from recess next week.
To support his claim, he singled out President Clinton's opposition to a welfare proposal by Texas Gov. George Bush that would effectively privatize that state's welfare system.

"There are some very, very disturbing indications that the Clinton administration is trying to undermine welfare reform," the Georgia Republican told reporters after visiting a public middle school in his home district.
"(Congress) may want to look at passing a law that would require them to accept proposals like Governor Bush's proposal," the speaker added.

Bush, the son of former President George Bush, wants to use private companies to determine eligibility for social service programs such as food stamps and Medicaid. He is a possible Republican contender for the White House in 2000.

Republican leaders including Gingrich have applauded the notion of giving the private sector a role in federal government assistance programs for the poor, but the White House has let it be known the Texas plan would not win full federal approval.

The Clinton administration, facing criticism from Democrats for signing welfare legislation passed by Congress last year, also has said former welfare recipients placed in community work programs must be covered by minimum wage laws.
State officials complain the higher wages could jeopardize the success of work programs by raising costs and undermining incentives for recipients to find private sector jobs.
